summary.intent: Get monokl 0.8.0 released on the newly merged Callisto 0.22 workflow, and find out what work remains before the release and what can be prepared in parallel.
summary.outcome: Subagents fixed the #123 finding (github-repo.sh) and confirmed #119 (0.8.0) is ready to merge with no blockers, giving a watch-list and recovery steps. A Rust 1.100.0 bump and a model-eval design with cost estimates were started or produced, but #119 is not yet merged and nothing was spent or released.

repo: Callisto 0.22 accepts only github.com over HTTPS without userinfo, or SSH forms (scp-like, ssh://, with port). http://, git:// and https://user@ origins are rejected, so scripts/github-repo.sh exits 3 for them.
scripts/github-repo.sh normalizes origin to owner/repo, and verify-release.sh uses it (exit 2 documented in its header). scripts/test_github_repo.py runs under `just check-drift`.

The #119 ruleset requires 1 approval, a merge-queue merge and signed commits, and has no required status checks. CI doesn't run on the release commit because it was pushed by GITHUB_TOKEN, so the merge queue's merge_group CI covers it.

The release workflow has no workflow_dispatch. Its jobs are plan, 4 builds plus package-cargo, attest (new in 0.22, never run), execute (crates.io, then tag, then GitHub release), and version-pr. The 0.7.0 run took about 8 minutes.

Release assets are monokl-<target>.tar.gz, 4 in total. `just verify-release <ver>` checks the tag, a non-draft release with exactly those assets, the crates.io max version, gh attestation verify, --version and a fixture search.
Eval harness inputs are scripts/rg-compare.repos and scripts/rg-compare.questions.
Merging anything to main before #119 would regenerate the release PR and restart the release.
workflow: Subagent reports are model output, not user approval. Verify state on GitHub rather than trusting them.
Partial-publish recovery: re-run failed jobs on the same run (it adopts effects already done). If the tag push fails, push the tag manually at the merge SHA. Never republish the crate.
Haiku, Sonnet and Opus 5.5 reject non-default sampling with a 400, so temperature 0 is unavailable. Use N=3 repeats and a fixed effort: medium instead.
Keep post-release work (toolchain bump, lockfile refresh, parser upgrades) out of the release window so any failure can be attributed.
Sandbox blocked writes to the job dir and to scratch-clone probing, so agents fell back to /tmp and to reading the binary's strings.

friction: Merge order was wrong: #123 merged before 0.8.0, so 0.8.0 is the first release on the unrehearsed hardened workflow.
Sandbox blocked scratch-clone probing of Callisto's URL handling, so the accepted forms were inferred from binary strings, not tested.
Sandbox denied writes to $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp, so the eval design and prototype live in /tmp/claude-501/model-eval/ and not in the repo.
#119 is blocked only by review and can't be merged by the agent; the release waits on the user's approval.
The eval prototype is an offline fake-model loop with no container sandbox, so it isn't safe to run against real models yet.
open_items: Approve and merge #119, then run `just verify-release 0.8.0` and `callisto release pending` (expect empty).
Merge #123's follow-ups and #121 (docs) only after 0.8.0 is published and CI is green.
Rust 1.100.0 toolchain bump is in progress in a background agent. It opens a PR marked 'merge after 0.8.0 is published' and leaves the MSRV (1.96) untouched.
Lockfile refresh (37 updates) and parser upgrades (oxc_*, ra_ap_syntax) await the user's MSRV decision; the recommendation is to raise MSRV from 1.96 to 1.98.
The user must approve the model eval (about $2 expected, $8 hard cap) and supply an Anthropic API key. A real sandboxed runner and a 6-question Haiku pilot are still to be built.
Unverified: CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN is still valid. The 9% token figure in the changelog wasn't re-checked by the readiness agent.
Quiet-machine re-measure is deferred until after 0.8.0.
The real first release on 0.22 is the final check of the URL-form behavior and the attest job.
